claim: The piriform cortex (PCx) receives direct input from the olfactory bulb (OB) and is the brain's main station for odor recognition and memory.
source: The piriform cortex (PCx) receives direct input from the olfactory bulb (OB) and is the brain's main station for odor recognition and memory.
evidence: This is a general statement about PCx function that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Mitral and tufted cells in olfactory glomeruli respond to individual odorant molecules.
source: The transformation of the odor code from OB to PCx is profound: mitral and tufted cells in olfactory glomeruli respond to individual odorant molecules, whereas pyramidal neurons (PNs) in the PCx responds to multiple, apparently random combinations of activated glomeruli.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about olfactory processing.

claim: Pyramidal neurons in the PCx respond to multiple, apparently random combinations of activated glomeruli.
source: The transformation of the odor code from OB to PCx is profound: mitral and tufted cells in olfactory glomeruli respond to individual odorant molecules, whereas pyramidal neurons (PNs) in the PCx responds to multiple, apparently random combinations of activated glomeruli.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about olfactory processing in PCx.

claim: NMDA spikes within individual dendrites can both amplify OB inputs and impose combination selectivity upon them.
source: Counter to the prevailing view that olfactory PNs sum their inputs passively, we show for the first time that NMDA spikes within individual dendrites can both amplify OB inputs and impose combination selectivity upon them, while their ability to compartmentalize voltage signals allows different dendrites to represent different odorant combinations.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The ability of dendrites to compartmentalize voltage signals allows different dendrites to represent different odorant combinations.
source: Counter to the prevailing view that olfactory PNs sum their inputs passively, we show for the first time that NMDA spikes within individual dendrites can both amplify OB inputs and impose combination selectivity upon them, while their ability to compartmentalize voltage signals allows different dendrites to represent different odorant combinations.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The 2-layer integrative behavior of olfactory PN dendrites provides a parsimonious account for the nonlinear remapping of the odor code from bulb to cortex.
source: Thus, the 2-layer integrative behavior of olfactory PN dendrites provides a parsimonious account for the nonlinear remapping of the odor code from bulb to cortex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and modeling results presented in the study.

claim: The piriform cortex is thought to be the brain's primary site for odor discrimination and recognition.
source: It receives direct odor information from the olfactory bulb, as well as contextual information from higher brain regions, and is thought to be the brain's primary site for odor discrimination and recognition (Gottfried, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: A single odor activates multiple odorant receptors at the nasal epithelium.
source: Olfaction starts at the nasal epithelium where a single odor activates multiple odorant receptors (ORs).
evidence: This reflects established knowledge about olfactory processing.

claim: Information from like ORs converge to ~1000 mirror symmetric pairs of glomeruli at the olfactory bulb.
source: At the olfactory bulb, information from like ORs converge to ~1000 mirror symmetric pairs of glomeruli (Mombaerts et al., 1996; Isaacson, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: On either side of the brain an odor is represented as a distributed pattern of activation over ~1000 glomeruli.
source: Thus, on either side of the brain an odor is represented as a distributed pattern of activation over ~1000 glomeruli, which together form a molecular map of the odor.
evidence: This is an inference based on the convergence of OR information to glomeruli.

claim: LOT axons traverse layer 1 of the PCx and form synaptic contacts with the thin distal dendrites of pyramidal neurons and layer 1 interneurons.
source: LOT axons traverse layer 1 of the PCx and form synaptic contacts with the thin distal dendrites of pyramidal neurons and layer 1 interneurons (Gottfried, 2010; Bekkers and Suzuki, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The connectivity scheme between the OB and PCx lacks any apparent spatial structure.
source: Unlike other sensory cortices which are topographically organized, the connectivity scheme between the OB and PCx lacks any apparent spatial structure: individual LOT axons from the bulb terminate in broad overlapping swaths of the PCx (Buonviso et al., 1991a; Buonviso et al., 1991b; Ojima et al., 1984; Miyamichi et al., 2011) so that each glomerulus excites a widely dispersed and apparently randomly distributed population of PCx neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Individual LOT axons from the bulb terminate in broad overlapping swaths of the PCx.
source: Unlike other sensory cortices which are topographically organized, the connectivity scheme between the OB and PCx lacks any apparent spatial structure: individual LOT axons from the bulb terminate in broad overlapping swaths of the PCx (Buonviso et al., 1991a; Buonviso et al., 1991b; Ojima et al., 1984; Miyamichi et al., 2011) so that each glomerulus excites a widely dispersed and apparently randomly distributed population of PCx neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Each glomerulus excites a widely dispersed and apparently randomly distributed population of PCx neurons.
source: Unlike other sensory cortices which are topographically organized, the connectivity scheme between the OB and PCx lacks any apparent spatial structure: individual LOT axons from the bulb terminate in broad overlapping swaths of the PCx (Buonviso et al., 1991a; Buonviso et al., 1991b; Ojima et al., 1984; Miyamichi et al., 2011) so that each glomerulus excites a widely dispersed and apparently randomly distributed population of PCx neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Each pyramidal neuron in PCx receives synaptic input from roughly ~10% of the 1000 glomeruli, also apparently randomly sampled.
source: In turn, each pyramidal neuron in PCx receives synaptic input from roughly ~10% of the 1000 glomeruli, also apparently randomly sampled (Miyamichi et al., 2011; Davison and Ehlers, 2011; Nagayama, 2010; Sosulski et al., 2011; Ghosh et al., 2011; Stettler and Axel, 2009; Soucy et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Each odorant activates an apparently random population of from 3% to 15% of the neurons in layer 2 of the PCx at low concentration.
source: In keeping with the notion of random convergence and divergence of OB axons in PCx, electrophysiological studies show that each odorant activates an apparently random population of from 3% to 15% of the neurons in layer 2 of the PCx at low concentration (Stettler and Axel, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Compartmentalized NMDA spikes in pyramidal neuron dendrites could provide both the thresholding nonlinearity that enforces combination selectivity, and the amplification that allows distal inputs to drive somatic action potentials.
source: A possible mechanism could be compartmentalized NMDA spikes in pyramidal neuron dendrites, which could provide both the thresholding nonlinearity that enforces combination selectivity, and the amplification that allows distal inputs to drive somatic action potentials (Poirazi et al., 2003; Polsky et al., 2004; Larkum et al., 2009; Sheffield and Dombeck, 2015; Losonczy and Magee, 2006; Nevian et al., 2007; Milojkovic et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations to previous work on dendritic spikes in other brain regions.

claim: Bathellier et al. reported that pyramidal neurons in PCx lack sufficient NMDA (or other) regenerative currents that could provide either the combination selectivity or amplification of LOT inputs.
source: Weighing against this hypothesis, however, the one study that has analyzed dendritic responses of olfactory PNs using current injections and focal electrical stimulation reported that pyramidal neurons in the PCx lack sufficient NMDA (or other) regenerative currents that could provide either the combination selectivity or amplification of LOT inputs (Bathellier et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement references findings from a previous study.

claim: Bathellier et al. reported that pyramidal neurons in PCx act as intrinsically linear summing units.
source: Rather, Bathellier et al. reported that pyramidal neurons in PCx, unlike their counterparts in other cortical areas, act as intrinsically linear summing units.
evidence: This statement references findings from a previous study.

claim: Apicella et al., 2010 found no reduction in a pyramidal neuron's combination selectivity when its IC inputs were blocked with baclofen.
source: Apicella et al., 2010 tested whether a pyramidal neuron's ability to respond selectively to LOT input combinations depends on IC inputs, which outnumber a pyramidal neuron's LOT inputs 10 to 1, but they found no reduction in a pyramidal neuron's combination selectively when its IC inputs were blocked with baclofen.
evidence: This statement references findings from a previous study.

claim: Robust NMDA spikes can be generated in dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons, both in layer 1a and layer two which receives direct LOT input.
source: We found that robust NMDA spikes can indeed be generated in dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons, both in layer 1a and layer two which receives direct LOT input, and using a model we show that these local spikes can effectively amplify clustered versus distributed LOT inputs forming the basis for a discontinuous receptive field.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Local NMDA spikes can effectively amplify clustered versus distributed LOT inputs forming the basis for a discontinuous receptive field.
source: We found that robust NMDA spikes can indeed be generated in dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons, both in layer 1a and layer two which receives direct LOT input, and using a model we show that these local spikes can effectively amplify clustered versus distributed LOT inputs forming the basis for a discontinuous receptive field.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling presented in the study.

claim: Supralinear summation of LOT inputs is largely confined to a single dendrite.
source: We also show that supralinear summation of LOT inputs is largely confined to a single dendrite, whereas nonlinear interactions of LOT inputs between dendrites are weak.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Nonlinear interactions of LOT inputs between dendrites are weak.
source: We also show that supralinear summation of LOT inputs is largely confined to a single dendrite, whereas nonlinear interactions of LOT inputs between dendrites are weak.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Interactions between LOT and IC inputs are nonlinear.
source: Finally, we show that interactions between LOT and IC inputs are also nonlinear, a fact that will likely be important for understanding the recurrent pattern completion functions of the PCx.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Gradually increasing the laser intensity to uncage glutamate evoked EPSP-like potentials, which increased progressively up to a threshold laser activation, beyond which a local spike was initiated.
source: Gradually increasing the laser intensity to uncage glutamate evoked EPSP-like potentials, which increased progressively up to a threshold laser activation, beyond which a local spike was initiated (Figure 1a–b; n = 10 cells).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Addition of the voltage-gated sodium channel blocker TTX (1 µm) did not significantly change the peak of the slow spikes (90.8 ± 6.0% of control; p = 0.16; n = 5).
source: Addition of the voltage-gated sodium channel blocker TTX (1 µm) did not significantly change the peak of the slow spikes (90.8 ± 6.0% of control; p = 0.16; n = 5).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with statistical analysis.

claim: An added cocktail of voltage-gated calcium channel blockers had a small, non-significant effect on the peak of the dendritic spike (85.4 ± 4.2% of control; p = 0.08; n = 5).
source: An added cocktail of voltage-gated calcium channel blockers (w-agatoxin 0.5 µM, conotoxin-GVIA 5 µM; SNX 482 200 nM, nifedipine10 µM) had a small, non-significant effect on the peak of the dendritic spike (85.4 ± 4.2% of control; p = 0.08; n = 5).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with statistical analysis.

claim: APV (2-amino 5-phosphonovalerate; 50 µM) a specific NMDAR channel blocker, completely abolished spike initiation.
source: Finally, APV (2-amino 5-phosphonovalerate; 50 µM) a specific NMDAR channel blocker, completely abolished spike initiation (Figure 1b–d).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: NMDA spikes can be initiated in dendrites of pyramidal neurons in PCx, as in fine dendrites of hippocampal and neocortical pyramidal neurons.
source: These results indicate that as in fine dendrites of hippocampal and neocortical pyramidal neurons (Stuart and Spruston, 2015; Major et al., 2013), NMDA spikes can be initiated in dendrites of pyramidal neurons in PCx.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and comparison with cited literature.

claim: Voltage gated sodium and calcium channels only minimally contributed to the slow component of the spike, while the majority of the current was carried by NMDAR channels.
source: Voltage gated sodium and calcium channels only minimally contributed to the slow component of the spike, while the majority of the current was carried by NMDAR channels (Major et al., 2008; Schiller et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and supported by citations.

claim: The average spike threshold evoked by LOT stimulation and recorded at the soma was 14.1 ± 1.6 mV.
source: The average spike threshold evoked by LOT stimulation and recorded at the soma was 14.1 ± 1.6 mV and the dendritic spike amplitude and area under the voltage curve (hereafter 'area') measured at the soma was 27.1 ± 2.4 mV and 3817.8 ± 396.9 mV*ms respectively (mean ± SD; n = 48 cells; stimulation location 276.78 ± 55 µm from soma).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The dendritic spike amplitude measured at the soma was 27.1 ± 2.4 mV.
source: The average spike threshold evoked by LOT stimulation and recorded at the soma was 14.1 ± 1.6 mV and the dendritic spike amplitude and area under the voltage curve (hereafter 'area') measured at the soma was 27.1 ± 2.4 mV and 3817.8 ± 396.9 mV*ms respectively (mean ± SD; n = 48 cells; stimulation location 276.78 ± 55 µm from soma).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The dendritic spike area measured at the soma was 3817.8 ± 396.9 mV*ms.
source: The average spike threshold evoked by LOT stimulation and recorded at the soma was 14.1 ± 1.6 mV and the dendritic spike amplitude and area under the voltage curve (hereafter 'area') measured at the soma was 27.1 ± 2.4 mV and 3817.8 ± 396.9 mV*ms respectively (mean ± SD; n = 48 cells; stimulation location 276.78 ± 55 µm from soma).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: APV (50 µM) blocked the initiation of dendritic spikes by LOT inputs and linearized stimulus-response curves.
source: In line with the uncaging data, APV (50 µM) blocked the initiation of dendritic spikes by LOT inputs and linearized stimulus-response curves (Figure 2c–e).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: At just-suprathreshold stimulus intensity, APV decreased the response peak and area by 56.3 ± 3.8% and 88.5 ± 2.6% respectively (n = 17).
source: At just-suprathreshold stimulus intensity, APV decreased the response peak and area by 56.3 ± 3.8% and 88.5 ± 2.6% respectively (n = 17).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: In 22% of neurons a fast initial spike component was recorded.
source: Also similar to uncaging, in 22% of neurons we recorded a fast initial spike component (Figure 2f; amplitude 13.322 ± 0.516 mV, threshold 9.71 ± 0.79 mV, n = 8; 217.14 ± 29 µm from soma).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from experimental data.

claim: The average resting membrane potential was relatively hyperpolarized (−80.1 ± 1.43 mV).
source: The average resting membrane potential was relatively hyperpolarized (−80.1 ± 1.43 mV), so that in many cases the NMDA spike remained subthreshold for somatic firing, however in some cases we could observe somatic firing as a result of the NMDA spike.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: Spontaneous spike-like events resembled synaptically evoked spikes in shape, including a clear inflection at spike initiation.
source: Occasionally we observed spontaneous spike-like events, which resembled synaptically evoked spikes in shape, including a clear inflection at spike initiation (Figure 2g–h).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The average spontaneous spike amplitude and area were 17.78 ± 2.09 mV and 9941 ± 2640 mV*ms respectively (n = 22 spikes).
source: The average spontaneous spike amplitude and area were 17.78 ± 2.09 mV and 9941 ± 2640 mV*ms respectively (n = 22 spikes).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: Addition of MK801 to the patch pipette solution completely blocked dendritic spikes.
source: Addition of MK801 to the patch pipette solution completely blocked dendritic spikes (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The spike amplitude and area at just-suprathreshold stimulation intensity was reduced to 32.7 ± 5.3% and 17.2 ± 2.2% respectively with intracellular MK801 (n = 6 cells; 40 min after patch breakthrough).
source: The spike amplitude and area at just-suprathreshold stimulation intensity was reduced to 32.7 ± 5.3% and 17.2 ± 2.2% respectively (n = 6 cells; 40 min after patch breakthrough).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: NMDA spikes were accompanied by large calcium transients around the activated dendritic site.
source: Dendritic calcium imaging revealed that NMDA spikes were accompanied by large calcium transients around the activated dendritic site (Figure 3).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Large calcium transients were seen only in the stimulated branches; calcium transients in unstimulated branches remained low.
source: Large calcium transients were seen only in the stimulated branches; calcium transients in unstimulated branches remained low (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: A maximal calcium transient at the activated dendritic location fell off steeply in both proximal and distal directions relative to the activated sites.
source: Using OGB-6F we observed a maximal calcium transient at the activated dendritic location which fell off steeply in both proximal and distal directions relative to the activated sites (Figure 3b–e).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The calcium profile data are consistent with NMDA spike-evoked calcium profiles seen in basal dendrites of layer five pyramidal neurons, and indicate the initiation of a local, non-actively propagated spike.
source: These data are consistent with NMDA spike-evoked calcium profiles seen in basal dendrites of layer five pyramidal neurons, and indicate the initiation of a local, non-actively propagated spike (Major et al., 2008; Schiller et al., 2000).
evidence: This is an interpretation of experimental data supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Pyramidal neurons in PCx receive a much larger number of inputs from IC axons in the deeper layers than from bulb inputs conveyed by the LOT in layer 1a.
source: In addition to bulb inputs conveyed by the LOT in layer 1a, pyramidal neurons in PCx receive a much larger number of inputs from IC axons in the deeper layers (Haberly, 2001; Haberly and Price, 1978; Johnson et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Spikes could be generated throughout the LOT-recipient zone in layer 1a, but also in layers 1b and two where pyramidal neurons primarily receive intracortical inputs.
source: We found that spikes could not only be generated throughout the LOT-recipient zone in layer 1a, but also in layers 1b and two where pyramidal neurons primarily receive intracortical inputs (Figure 4).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The amplitude of NMDA spikes recorded at the soma increased significantly (from 6.4 ± 0.7 mV to 25.9 ± 3.1 mV) as the uncaging site moved from distal (318.6 ± 7.9 µm) to proximal (99 ± 14.6 µm) dendritic locations (p = 0.00014).
source: In keeping with previous reports (Major et al., 2008), the amplitude of NMDA spikes recorded at the soma increased significantly (from 6.4 ± 0.7 mV to 25.9 ± 3.1 mV) as the uncaging site moved from distal (318.6 ± 7.9 µm) to proximal (99 ± 14.6 µm) dendritic locations (Figure 4c; p = 0.00014).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: The apical dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons are capable of generating spikes throughout the layers that receive LOT and IC inputs.
source: Thus, the apical dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons are capable of generating spikes throughout the layers that receive LOT and IC inputs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: When dendritic spikes were initiated at distal dendritic locations using synaptic stimulation (254.85 ± 14.95 µm from soma), addition of baclofen only slightly altered spike amplitude (spike amplitude was reduced by 10.4 ± 7.3%, p = 0.02 and spike threshold increased by 10.1 ± 12.6%, p = 0.004, n = 6).
source: When dendritic spikes were initiated at distal dendritic locations using synaptic stimulation (254.85 ± 14.95 µm from soma), addition of baclofen only slightly altered spike amplitude (Figure 4d–e; spike amplitude was reduced by 10.4 ± 7.3%, p = 0.02 and spike threshold increased by 10.1 ± 12.6%, p = 0.004, n = 6).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: At mid dendritic locations (197.3 ± 12 µm), local spikes were evidently triggered by a mixture of LOT and intracortical inputs, since upon baclofen application, response amplitude was reduced (peak voltage response was reduced by 42.0 ± 13.3%, compared to control; n = 6).
source: At mid dendritic locations (197.3 ± 12 µm), local spikes were evidently triggered by a mixture of LOT and intracortical inputs, since upon baclofen application, response amplitude was reduced (peak voltage response was reduced by 42.0 ± 13.3%, compared to control; n = 6).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with quantitative measurements and interpretation.

claim: At more proximal locations (161.6 ± 9.6 µm) spike initiation was almost completely dependent on intracortical inputs: when baclofen was present, we were unable to initiate local spikes at all, and the voltage response was significantly reduced (peak response was reduced by 63.2 ± 6.2%, compared to control; n = 6).
source: At more proximal locations (161.6 ± 9.6 µm) spike initiation was almost completely dependent on intracortical inputs: when baclofen was present, we were unable to initiate local spikes at all, and the voltage response was significantly reduced (Figure 4f–g; peak response was reduced by 63.2 ± 6.2%, compared to control; n = 6).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with quantitative measurements and interpretation.

claim: At all dendritic locations, addition of APV (50 µm) completely abolished spike initiation.
source: At all dendritic locations, addition of APV (50 µm) completely abolished spike initiation (Figure 4d–h).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Pyramidal neurons in PCx are capable of NMDA spike generation throughout their apical arbors.
source: Taken together these results indicate that pyramidal neurons in PCx are capable of NMDA spike generation throughout their apical arbors; that both LOT and IC inputs can generate NMDA spikes within their respective layers; and that these synaptically evoked dendritic spikes show the commonly observed increase in amplitude as the initiation site moves closer to the soma (Major et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: Both LOT and IC inputs can generate NMDA spikes within their respective layers.
source: Taken together these results indicate that pyramidal neurons in PCx are capable of NMDA spike generation throughout their apical arbors; that both LOT and IC inputs can generate NMDA spikes within their respective layers; and that these synaptically evoked dendritic spikes show the commonly observed increase in amplitude as the initiation site moves closer to the soma (Major et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: Synaptically evoked dendritic spikes show the commonly observed increase in amplitude as the initiation site moves closer to the soma.
source: Taken together these results indicate that pyramidal neurons in PCx are capable of NMDA spike generation throughout their apical arbors; that both LOT and IC inputs can generate NMDA spikes within their respective layers; and that these synaptically evoked dendritic spikes show the commonly observed increase in amplitude as the initiation site moves closer to the soma (Major et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and supported by citation.

claim: Coactivation of two inputs on the same dendrite resulted in a strong nonlinear interaction, where Input two significantly lowered the threshold for local spike generation by Input 1 (by 46.55 ± 1.8% for peak voltage; t-test p < 0.0001 and 52 degrees of freedom; F-score of 2.36).
source: Coactivation of the two inputs resulted in a strong nonlinear interaction, where Input two significantly lowered the threshold for local spike generation by Input 1 (by 46.55 ± 1.8% for peak voltage; t-test p < 0.0001 and 52 degrees of freedom; F-score of 2.36; Figure 5a–d) without changing the response peak amplitude.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: The nonlinear interaction between LOT inputs delivered to two different branches, even when those branches were 'sisters', was much weaker than the within-branch interaction, as evidenced by the much smaller change in spike threshold caused by the bias input (7.98 ± 0.75%, n = 5 threshold change for the sister-branch and 6.28 ± 1.88%, n = 6 threshold change for the different-branch).
source: We found in favor of this hypothesis, that the nonlinear interaction between LOT inputs delivered to two different branches, even when those branches were 'sisters' (Figure 5c–e), was much weaker than the within-branch interaction, as evidenced by the much smaller change in spike threshold caused by the bias input (7.98 ± 0.75%, n = 5 threshold change for the sister-branch and 6.28 ± 1.88%, n = 6 threshold change for the different-branch, Figure 5c–e).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: An ANOVA test for comparison between the three groups (same, sister, different branches) showed statistical significance (p < 0.01).
source: An ANOVA test for comparison between the three groups (same, sister, different branches) showed statistical significance (p < 0.01).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Post-hoc analysis (Tukey-Kramer test) comparing each group with every other group yielded significant differences between same branch and sister and different branches (p < 0.01), but no statistical significance between sister and different branches (p = 0.98).
source: Post-hoc analysis (Tukey-Kramer test) comparing each group with every other group yielded significant differences between same branch and sister and different branches (p < 0.01), but no statistical significance between sister and different branches (p = 0.98).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: In the pairing experiments in the presence of APV, the bias added a roughly constant value to the unpaired voltage response (Control + APV) all along the curve, confirming that without NMDA channels, pyramidal neuron dendrites revert to roughly linear summation.
source: To more closely examine the role of NMDA channels in the pairing outcomes, we repeated the pairing experiments in the presence of APV (Figure 5c–d). In these cases, the bias added a roughly constant value to the unpaired voltage response (Control + APV) all along the curve, confirming that without NMDA channels, pyramidal neuron dendrites revert to roughly linear summation.
evidence: This is an experimental observation and interpretation.

claim: The threshold was lowered by 52.2 ± 2.34% and 15.6 ± 4.2% when the synaptic bias was located on the same or different branches, respectively, in glutamate uncaging experiments.
source: Similar to the previous two-electrode summation experiments, we observed a significant difference between same and different branch summation. The threshold was lowered by 52.2 ± 2.34% and 15.6 ± 4.2% when the synaptic bias was located on the same or different branches, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: NMDA spike generation in the distal apical dendrites of pyramidal neurons provides the superlinearity needed to enforce selectivity for specific combinations of LOT inputs.
source: Together these results support a model of olfactory coding in PCx in which (1) NMDA spike generation in the distal apical dendrites of pyramidal neurons provides the superlinearity needed to enforce selectivity for specific combinations of LOT inputs, while the compartmentalization of voltage signals in the apical tree allows for different LOT combinations to be mapped onto different apical dendrites with relatively little crosstalk between them.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and modeling.

claim: The compartmentalization of voltage signals in the apical tree allows for different LOT combinations to be mapped onto different apical dendrites with relatively little crosstalk between them.
source: Together these results support a model of olfactory coding in PCx in which (1) NMDA spike generation in the distal apical dendrites of pyramidal neurons provides the superlinearity needed to enforce selectivity for specific combinations of LOT inputs, while the compartmentalization of voltage signals in the apical tree allows for different LOT combinations to be mapped onto different apical dendrites with relatively little crosstalk between them.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and modeling.

claim: Summation of LOT and IC inputs was very similar in form to the summation of two inputs confined to the LOT: the IC bias input again led to a substantial threshold reduction for LOT inputs (35.44 ± 2.0%, n = 15), with no increase in response magnitude.
source: We found that summation of LOT and IC inputs was very similar in form to the summation of two inputs confined to the LOT (Figure 6a–e): the IC bias input again led to a substantial threshold reduction for LOT inputs (35.44 ± 2.0%, n = 15), with no increase in response magnitude.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The threshold-lowering effect of the bias input was relatively constant within increasing separation of the two inputs, indicating that over much of its length, a pyramidal neuron apical dendrite functions as a single, relatively location-insensitive integrative subunit.
source: Indeed, the threshold-lowering effect of the bias input was relatively constant within increasing separation of the two inputs (Figure 6f), indicating that over much of its length, a pyramidal neuron apical dendrite functions as a single, relatively location-insensitive integrative subunit.
evidence: This is an interpretation of experimental data.

claim: Blocking NMDARs linearized the input-output curves, destroying their sigmoidal form, and eliminating the basis for a superlinear within–branch interactions.
source: We also found that, just as for pairs of inputs confined to the LOT, the nonlinear interaction between LOT and IC inputs depended completely on NMDA regenerativity: blocking NMDARs linearized the input-output curves, destroying their sigmoidal form, and eliminating the basis for a superlinear within–branch interactions (Figure 6, grey curves).
evidence: This is an experimental observation and interpretation.

claim: When the bias was provided by an IC input on a sister branch, the nonlinear interaction was evident, though significantly weaker compared to that seen with a same-branch IC bias (threshold reduction was 23.38 ± 2.34%, n = 8).
source: When the bias was provided by an IC input on a sister branch, the nonlinear interaction was evident, though significantly weaker compared to that seen with a same-branch IC bias (Figure 7a–b,e). Threshold reduction was 23.38 ± 2.34% (n = 8) for IC locations on sister branches and 18.4 ± 2.88% (n = 7) for IC bias on different branch (Figure 7c–e).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: Threshold reduction was 18.4 ± 2.88% (n = 7) for IC bias on different branch.
source: Threshold reduction was 23.38 ± 2.34% (n = 8) for IC locations on sister branches and 18.4 ± 2.88% (n = 7) for IC bias on different branch (Figure 7c–e).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The model cell can generate NMDA spikes in response to concentrated synaptic excitation at any location along a pyramidal neuron's apical dendrite.
source: We first established that the model cell can generate NMDA spikes in response to concentrated synaptic excitation at any location along a pyramidal neuron's apical dendrite, and that both the threshold for spike initiation and the spike amplitude measured at the soma increase as the site of spike initiation moves closer to the soma (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling.

claim: Both the threshold for spike initiation and the spike amplitude measured at the soma increase as the site of spike initiation moves closer to the soma in the model.
source: We first established that the model cell can generate NMDA spikes in response to concentrated synaptic excitation at any location along a pyramidal neuron's apical dendrite, and that both the threshold for spike initiation and the spike amplitude measured at the soma increase as the site of spike initiation moves closer to the soma (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling.

claim: The model supports the experimental finding that nonlinear synaptic summation of LOT inputs to distal apical dendrites is strongly compartmentalized, with individual apical dendrites acting as well-separated integrative subunits.
source: Thus, the model supports our experimental finding that nonlinear synaptic summation of LOT inputs to distal apical dendrites is strongly compartmentalized, with individual apical dendrites acting as well-separated integrative subunits.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from computational modeling results.

claim: The model replicated the experimental finding that IC bias inputs on sister and different branches had a significantly weaker effect than an IC bias on the same branch.
source: In addition, the model replicated the experimental finding that IC bias inputs on sister and different branches had a significantly weaker effect than an IC bias on the same branch (compare Figure 8—figure supplement 2g to Figure 8d), though the degree of compartmentalization of IC inputs was, as in the experiments, and as expected from passive cable theory, less pronounced than the compartmentalization of LOT inputs.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling that replicates experimental results.

claim: The degree of compartmentalization of IC inputs was less pronounced than the compartmentalization of LOT inputs.
source: In addition, the model replicated the experimental finding that IC bias inputs on sister and different branches had a significantly weaker effect than an IC bias on the same branch (compare Figure 8—figure supplement 2g to Figure 8d), though the degree of compartmentalization of IC inputs was, as in the experiments, and as expected from passive cable theory, less pronounced than the compartmentalization of LOT inputs.
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling and experimental data.

claim: Simulations revealed strong supralinear LOT and IC input summation when either of the inputs was temporally shifted by 20 ms, and in some cases more.
source: These nonlinear synaptic interactions persisted for non-synchronized inputs: our simulations revealed strong supralinear LOT and IC input summation when either of the inputs was temporally shifted by 20 ms, and in some cases more (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling.

claim: The model supports the experimental findings that IC inputs interact nonlinearly with LOT inputs over extended spatio-temporal scales.
source: Thus, the model supports our experimental findings that IC inputs interact nonlinearly with LOT inputs over extended spatio-temporal scales.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from computational modeling results.

claim: Clustered LOT inputs reliably evoked NMDA spikes, powerfully amplifying postsynaptic signal compared to Ohmic (voltage-independent) NMDAR.
source: As predicted, we found that that clustered LOT inputs reliably evoked NMDA spikes, powerfully amplifying postsynaptic signal compared to Ohmic (voltage-independent) NMDAR (Figure 8c).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling.

claim: Dispersed LOT activation typically failed to overcome the local spike threshold on any dendrite, due both to the lack of concentrated excitation and the presence of inhibition, and therefore resulted in significantly smaller local dendritic and somatic voltage responses.
source: In contrast, dispersed LOT activation typically failed to overcome the local spike threshold on any dendrite, due both to the lack of concentrated excitation and the presence of inhibition, and therefore resulted in significantly smaller local dendritic and somatic voltage responses (Figure 8b–d, pink).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling.

claim: The difference between clustered and dispersed synaptic distributions was evident over a large input range, leading to preferential amplification of input combinations that target individual postsynaptic branches.
source: The difference between clustered and dispersed synaptic distributions was evident over a large input range (Figure 8c–d), leading to preferential amplification of input combinations that target individual postsynaptic branches (Figure 8c).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling.

claim: Stimulation with Ohmic NMDARs eliminated the strong dependence of postsynaptic responses on the spatial distribution of synaptic inputs.
source: This effect was entirely dependent on regenerative NMDAR currents: stimulation with Ohmic NMDARs, eliminated the strong dependence of postsynaptic responses on the spatial distribution of synaptic inputs (Figure 8c, inset,).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling.

claim: The AB combination produced strong supralinear responses, whereas the AC combination produced only a weak depolarization and mostly linear or sublinear summation in the model.
source: We found the AB combination produced strong supralinear responses (Figure 8f left, g, black), whereas the AC combination produced only a weak depolarization and mostly linear or sublinear summation (Figure 8f, right, g, pink).
evidence: This is a finding from computational modeling.

claim: Even in the presence of significant trial-to-trial variability introduced by random background activity and biologically-realistic presynaptic firing patterns, the model olfactory pyramidal neuron was able to use clustered glomerular activation as a basis for representing certain 'odor' combinations but not others.
source: Thus, even in the presence of significant trial-to-trial variability introduced by random background activity and biologically-realistic presynaptic firing patterns, the model olfactory pyramidal neuron was able to use clustered glomerular activation as a basis for representing certain 'odor' combinations but not others (Figure 8h).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from computational modeling results.

claim: Pyramidal neurons in PCx can generate local spikes throughout their apical dendrites.
source: We found that pyramidal neurons in PCx can generate local spikes throughout their apical dendrites, and that a spike in a dendritic branch can powerfully depolarize the soma (i.e. producing up to 40–50 mV depolarizations depending on distance and cell size).
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings.

claim: A spike in a dendritic branch can powerfully depolarize the soma (i.e. producing up to 40–50 mV depolarizations depending on distance and cell size).
source: We found that pyramidal neurons in PCx can generate local spikes throughout their apical dendrites, and that a spike in a dendritic branch can powerfully depolarize the soma (i.e. producing up to 40–50 mV depolarizations depending on distance and cell size).
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings.

claim: The majority of dendritic spikes observed in PCx pyramidal neurons are mediated primarily by NMDAR channels similar to thin dendrites in other pyramidal neurons.
source: Our results are consistent with two key properties of local spikes seen in thin (basal, apical oblique, and tuft) dendrites of pyramidal neurons in other cortical areas. First, the majority of dendritic spikes we observed in PCx pyramidal neurons are mediated primarily by NMDAR channels similar to thin dendrites in other pyramidal neurons (Polsky et al., 2004; Larkum et al., 2009; Nevian et al., 2007; Lavzin et al., 2012; Antic et al., 2010; Schiller et al., 2000; Ariav et al., 2003; Major et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and comparison with cited literature.

claim: The logic of synaptic integration in pyramidal neuron dendrites in PCx, particularly the pronounced difference between same-branch and between-branch summation, is consistent with that seen in other types of pyramidal neurons.
source: Beyond the properties of NMDA spikes per se, we found that the logic of synaptic integration in pyramidal neuron dendrites in PCx, particularly the pronounced difference between same-branch and between-branch summation, is also consistent with that seen in other types of pyramidal neurons (Poo and Isaacson, 2009; Poirazi et al., 2003; Archie and Mel, 2000).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and comparison with cited literature.

claim: Synaptic inputs to a PCx pyramidal neurons are processed via a 2-layer computation.
source: In particular, synaptic inputs to a PCx pyramidal neurons are processed via a 2-layer computation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and modeling.

claim: LOT inputs are combined within individual dendrites as roughly a weighted sum (i.e. linearly) up to the local spike threshold.
source: First, LOT inputs are combined within individual dendrites as roughly a weighted sum (i.e. linearly) up to the local spike threshold (Figure 2d), so that an individual dendrite behaves comparably to a 'neuron' in a conventional artificial neural network.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: An individual dendrite behaves comparably to a 'neuron' in a conventional artificial neural network.
source: First, LOT inputs are combined within individual dendrites as roughly a weighted sum (i.e. linearly) up to the local spike threshold (Figure 2d), so that an individual dendrite behaves comparably to a 'neuron' in a conventional artificial neural network.
evidence: This is an interpretation of experimental data.

claim: In the second layer of processing, the outflows from the separately thresholded dendritic 'subunits' are combined linearly at the soma as a prelude to output spike generation.
source: In the second layer of processing, the outflows from the separately thresholded dendritic 'subunits' are combined linearly at the soma as a prelude to output spike generation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and modeling.

claim: The 2-layer architecture of a pyramidal neuron in PCx allows it to respond selectively to specific high-order odorant combinations – those whose LOT activity patterns deliver concentrated (suprathreshold) excitation to at least one apical dendrite – without responding to the vast majority of LOT patterns that produce more diffuse, and therefore subthreshold, excitation to multiple branches within the dendritic arbor.
source: The 2-layer architecture of a pyramidal neuron in PCx allows it to respond selectively to specific high-order odorant combinations – those whose LOT activity patterns deliver concentrated (suprathreshold) excitation to at least one apical dendrite – without responding to the vast majority of LOT patterns that produce more diffuse, and therefore subthreshold, excitation to multiple branches within the dendritic arbor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and modeling.

claim: The ability to respond to multiple distinct high-order combinations, without responding to re-combinations of the same odor components, may account for this cell type's hallmark physiological property, namely its 'discontinuous' receptive field.
source: This ability to respond to multiple distinct high-order combinations, without responding to re-combinations of the same odor components, may account for this cell type's hallmark physiological property, namely its 'discontinuous' receptive field (Stettler and Axel, 2009; Rennaker et al., 2007; Kadohisa and Wilson, 2006; Poo and Isaacson, 2009).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and modeling, supported by citations.

claim: The results showing that pyramidal neurons in PCx have a 2-layer summation logic arising from (1) NMDA regenerativity and (2) a compartmentalized dendritic tree, are inconsistent with a previous study which reported little sign of regenerative NMDA or sodium currents in pyramidal neuron dendrites.
source: As previously discussed, our results showing that pyramidal neurons in PCx have a 2-layer summation logic arising from (1) NMDA regenerativity and (2) a compartmentalized dendritic tree, are inconsistent with a previous study in olfactory cortex which reported little sign of regenerative NMDA or sodium currents in pyramidal neuron dendrites, and concluded that pyramidal neurons in PCx integrate their inputs essentially linearly (Bathellier et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current study's findings with previous work.

claim: The anatomical projection from the olfactory bulb to the cortex is generally assumed to be random.
source: Lacking any evidence for a patterning of these connections, the anatomical projection from the olfactory bulb to the cortex is generally assumed to be random.
evidence: This reflects current understanding in the field.

claim: Different odors activate a unique set of neurons widely distributed across the PCx.
source: In keeping with this assumption, physiological data show that different odors activate a unique set of neurons widely distributed across the PCx, and that individual olfactory pyramidal neurons respond to a small, unpredictable subset of odors (Stettler and Axel, 2009; Roland et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Individual olfactory pyramidal neurons respond to a small, unpredictable subset of odors.
source: In keeping with this assumption, physiological data show that different odors activate a unique set of neurons widely distributed across the PCx, and that individual olfactory pyramidal neurons respond to a small, unpredictable subset of odors (Stettler and Axel, 2009; Roland et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The transformation from molecule-specific responses in olfactory glomeruli to multi-combination selectivity in pyramidal neurons in PCx requires a nonlinear transformation.
source: This transformation from molecule-specific responses in olfactory glomeruli to multi-combination selectivity in pyramidal neurons in PCx requires a nonlinear transformation, and indeed several in-vivo and in-vitro studies have indicated that single pyramidal neurons in PCx do integrate odor information nonlinearly (Davison and Ehlers, 2011; Stettler and Axel, 2009; Apicella et al., 2010; Poo and Isaacson, 2011).
evidence: This is a logical inference supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Several in-vivo and in-vitro studies have indicated that single pyramidal neurons in PCx do integrate odor information nonlinearly.
source: This transformation from molecule-specific responses in olfactory glomeruli to multi-combination selectivity in pyramidal neurons in PCx requires a nonlinear transformation, and indeed several in-vivo and in-vitro studies have indicated that single pyramidal neurons in PCx do integrate odor information nonlinearly (Davison and Ehlers, 2011; Stettler and Axel, 2009; Apicella et al., 2010; Poo and Isaacson, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Activation of a single glomerulus or LOT fiber generates only a small subthreshold depolarization in most connected PCx pyramidal neurons.
source: In particular, activation of a single glomerulus or LOT fiber generates only a small subthreshold depolarization in most connected PCx pyramidal neurons.
evidence: This reflects established knowledge in the field.

claim: When multiple glomeruli or multiple LOT inputs are activated simultaneously, or combinations of odorants are presented to an animal, PCx pyramidal neurons produce strong supralinear responses.
source: On the other hand, when multiple glomeruli or multiple LOT inputs are activated simultaneously, or combinations of odorants are presented to an animal, PCx pyramidal neurons produce strong supralinear responses (Davison and Ehlers, 2011; Stettler and Axel, 2009; Kadohisa and Wilson, 2006; Apicella et al., 2010; Wilson, 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Apicella et al showed that the supralinear summation of LOT inputs onto pyramidal neurons, required neither cooperative interactions in the bulb, nor participation of recurrent IC inputs in PCx.
source: Apicella et al (Apicella et al., 2010). showed that the supralinear summation of LOT inputs onto pyramidal neurons, required neither cooperative interactions in the bulb, nor participation of recurrent IC inputs in PCx.
evidence: This statement references findings from a previous study.

claim: The results support the idea that the dendritic thresholding nonlinearity provided primarily by regenerative NMDA currents can mediate the supralinear integration of LOT inputs observed previously both in-vitro and in vivo.
source: In contrast, our results support the idea that the dendritic thresholding nonlinearity provided primarily by regenerative NMDA currents can mediate the supralinear integration of LOT inputs observed previously both in-vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and comparison with previous work.

claim: IC inputs are closer to the branch points where sister and cousin dendrites connect to each other, so that their effects are felt more widely.
source: The effect can be traced to passive cable theory: IC inputs are closer to the branch points where sister and cousin dendrites connect to each other, so that their effects are felt more widely.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on passive cable theory.

claim: The threshold-lowering power of a second LOT input on the same branch was roughly 10 times that of an LOT input delivered to a different branch.
source: In quantitative terms, beginning with a 'control' input-output curve generated by an LOT input, we found that the threshold-lowering power of a second LOT input on the same branch was roughly 10 times that of an LOT input delivered to a different branch.
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of experimental findings.

claim: The threshold-lowering effect of an IC bias input on the same branch is only twice that of an IC bias delivered to a different branch.
source: In contrast to this strong compartmentalization, the threshold-lowering effect of an IC bias input on the same branch is only twice that of an IC bias delivered to a different branch (Figure 7e).
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of experimental findings.

claim: The degree of nonlinear crosstalk between dendritic branches tends to be overestimated in subthreshold summation experiments, compared to a cell operating in the firing regime which enhances subunit independence.
source: The observation that IC inputs modulate more globally comes with a caveat, however: it was previously shown that the degree of nonlinear crosstalk between dendritic branches tends to be overestimated in subthreshold summation experiments, compared to a cell operating in the firing regime which enhances subunit independence (Behabadi and Mel, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The somatic spike-generating mechanism acts as a sort of time-averaged 'voltage clamp' that suppresses subthreshold voltage communication between dendrites.
source: This is because the somatic spike-generating mechanism acts as a sort of time-averaged 'voltage clamp' (Holt and Koch, 1997) that suppresses subthreshold voltage communication between dendrites (Behabadi and Mel, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: IC inputs provide contextual information from higher-order cortical regions including the entorhinal cortex, orbitofrontal cortex and amygdala, potentially allowing the assignment of cognitive and emotional value to odors.
source: Besides carrying feedback from other pyramidal neurons in the area, IC inputs provide contextual information from higher-order cortical regions including the entorhinal cortex, orbitofrontal cortex and amygdala, potentially allowing the assignment of cognitive and emotional value to odors (Gottfried, 2010; Johnson et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The nonlinear interaction of LOT and IC inputs mediated by NMDA regenerativity could provide a biophysical mechanism for binding odor with contextual information in piriform cortex.
source: The nonlinear interaction of LOT and IC inputs mediated by NMDA regenerativity could provide a biophysical mechanism for binding odor with contextual information in piriform cortex.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on experimental findings.

claim: Backpropagating action potentials in apical dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons attenuate significantly as they propagate.
source: Backpropagating action potentials in apical dendrites of PCx pyramidal neurons attenuate significantly as they propagate (Bathellier et al., 2009; Johenning et al., 2009), making it less likely that bAPs contribute to spike timing dependent plasticity of distal LOT synapses.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: NMDA currents can produce large localized calcium transients in apical dendrites, confined to within ±20 µm of the activated site.
source: In contrast, given that NMDA currents can produce large localized calcium transients in apical dendrites, confined to within ±20 µm of the activated site, such spikes could serve as local induction signals for plasticity of LOT synapses.

source: In accordance with this notion, it was recently shown that NMDA spikes contribute to long-term potentiation (LTP) in the dendrites of CA3 neurons (Brandalise and Gerber, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

source: In the same way, a group of LOT synapses that fire together on the same dendrite in PCx could trigger a local plasticity event that induces LTP of the activated synapses.
